title: CDL Hazmat shipping papers and emergency information practice questions
description: Free CDL Hazmat practice questions on shipping papers and emergency response information in 49 CFR 172. Every answer is explained and linked to its section.

questions.question: Under 172.200(a), who must describe a hazardous material on the shipping paper?

options.A: The driver who picks up the load at the shipper's dock
options.B: Each person who offers the hazardous material for transportation
options.C: The consignee who receives the shipment
options.D: The operator of the facility where the material is stored

questions.explanation: Section 172.200(a) states that, "Except as otherwise provided in this subpart, each person who offers a hazardous material for transportation shall describe the hazardous material on the shipping paper in the manner required by this subpart."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.200, Applicability (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A shipper offers a limited quantity package for transportation by highway. The material is not a hazardous substance, hazardous waste or marine pollutant. What does 172.200(b) say about Subpart C (shipping papers)?

options.A: A full shipping paper is always required for limited quantities
options.B: A shipping paper is required only when the package weighs more than 454 kg
options.C: Subpart C does not apply to it, because it is not offered for transportation by aircraft or vessel
options.D: Only the emergency response telephone number must be written on the package

questions.explanation: Subpart C "does not apply to any material, other than a hazardous substance, hazardous waste or marine pollutant, that is" a "limited quantity package unless the material is offered for transportation by aircraft or vessel."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.200, Applicability (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A shipping paper lists a hazardous material and a material not subject to the hazardous materials regulations. Which is one of the ways 172.201(a)(1) allows the hazardous material entries to be shown?

options.A: Entered first on the shipping paper
options.B: Entered last, after all other materials
options.C: Written on the back of the shipping paper
options.D: Entered in the same color as the other entries, with no other marking

questions.explanation: Under 172.201(a)(1) the hazardous material entries "Must be entered first," or "Must be entered in a color that clearly contrasts with any description on the shipping paper of a material not subject to the requirements of this subchapter," or be identified by an X in a column captioned HM.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.201, Preparation and retention of shipping papers (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: For a hazardous material that is not a hazardous waste, which retention period does 172.201(e) set for the copy kept by the person who provides the shipping paper?

options.A: One year after delivery to the consignee
options.B: Three years after the material is accepted by the initial carrier
options.C: Until the shipment is delivered
options.D: Two years after the material is accepted by the initial carrier

questions.explanation: "For all other hazardous materials, the shipping paper must be retained for two years after the material is accepted by the initial carrier." The three-year period applies "For a hazardous waste".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.201, Preparation and retention of shipping papers (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A motor carrier uses one shipping paper without change for many shipments of a hazardous material with the same shipping name and identification number. What does 172.201(e) allow?

options.A: Retaining a single copy of the shipping paper, if the carrier also retains a record of each shipment made
options.B: Keeping no copy, because the shipper already keeps one
options.C: Retaining a single copy with no other record
options.D: Keeping each copy only until the end of the trip

questions.explanation: Such a motor carrier "may retain a single copy of the shipping paper, instead of a copy for each shipment made, if the carrier also retains a record of each shipment made, to include shipping name, identification number, quantity transported, and date of shipment."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.201, Preparation and retention of shipping papers (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: The basic description and its sequence
questions.question: In which order does 172.202(b) require the parts of the basic description to be shown?

options.A: Proper shipping name, identification number, hazard class, packing group
options.B: Hazard class, proper shipping name, identification number, packing group
options.C: Identification number, proper shipping name, hazard class or division, packing group
options.D: Packing group, hazard class, identification number, proper shipping name

questions.explanation: The basic description in 172.202(a)(1) to (4) (identification number, proper shipping name, hazard class or division, packing group) "must be shown in sequence with no additional information interspersed", as in the rule's example "UN2744, Cyclobutyl chloroformate, 6.1, (8, 3), PG II."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.202, Description of hazardous material on shipping papers (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: The basic description and its sequence
questions.question: Which materials does 172.202(a)(4) except from showing a packing group in the basic description?

options.A: Class 3 materials assigned a packing group in Column (5)
options.B: Class 8 materials assigned a packing group in Column (5)
options.C: Division 6.1 materials assigned a packing group in Column (5)
options.D: Division 5.2 materials

questions.explanation: "Class 1 (explosives) materials; self-reactive substances; Division 5.2 materials; and entries that are not assigned a packing group (e.g., Class 7) are excepted from this requirement."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.202, Description of hazardous material on shipping papers (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: The basic description and its sequence
questions.question: A hazardous material is shipped by highway in one cargo tank. Under the bulk package exception in 172.202(a)(5)(iii), how may the total quantity be shown?

options.A: As the net explosive mass
options.B: By some indication of the total quantity, for example 1 cargo tank
options.C: As the gross mass per package followed by the letter G
options.D: No indication of quantity is needed at all

questions.explanation: Bulk packages are excepted from the total quantity requirement of 172.202(a)(5), "provided some indication of the total quantity is shown"; the rule's example is 1 cargo tank.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.202, Description of hazardous material on shipping papers (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A material is poisonous by inhalation. What does 172.203(m) require on the shipping paper immediately following the shipping description?

options.A: The words Poison-Inhalation Hazard or Toxic-Inhalation Hazard and the appropriate zone
options.B: The word HOT
options.C: The words Limited Quantity
options.D: The words Marine Pollutant

questions.explanation: "Notwithstanding the hazard class to which a material is assigned", for materials poisonous by inhalation the inhalation hazard words and the zone, as appropriate, "shall be entered on the shipping paper immediately following the shipping description."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.203, Additional description requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 172.203(h), what is entered after the basic description for noncorrosive liquefied petroleum gas in a Specification MC 330 or MC 331 cargo tank?

options.A: 0.2 PERCENT WATER
options.B: NOT FOR Q and T TANKS
options.C: HOT
options.D: NONCORROSIVE or NONCOR

questions.explanation: "Following the basic description for a hazardous material in a Specification MC 330 or MC 331 cargo tank", noncorrosive liquefied petroleum gas gets NONCORROSIVE or NONCOR; "NOT FOR Q and T TANKS" is for "grades of liquefied petroleum gas other than" noncorrosive, and 0.2 PERCENT WATER is an anhydrous ammonia entry.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.203, Additional description requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which shipment does 172.204(b)(1) except from the shipper's certification?

options.A: Any hazardous waste hauled in a cargo tank supplied by the carrier
options.B: A hazardous material, other than a hazardous waste, offered for transportation by motor vehicle and transported in a cargo tank supplied by the carrier
options.C: Any shipment of less than 454 kg
options.D: Any shipment hauled by a for-hire motor carrier

questions.explanation: "Except for a hazardous waste, no certification is required for a hazardous material offered for transportation by motor vehicle and transported:" "In a cargo tank supplied by the carrier", or by the shipper as a private carrier (with a limit for reshipped or transferred material).

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.204, Shipper's certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A shipper hauls its own hazardous material (not a hazardous waste) in non-bulk packages by motor vehicle as a private carrier, but the material will be transferred to another carrier to finish the trip. Under 172.204, is the shipper's certification required?

options.A: No, because the shipper is hauling as a private carrier
options.B: No, because all shipments by motor vehicle are excepted
options.C: Yes, because the private carrier exception does not cover material that is to be reshipped or transferred from one carrier to another
options.D: Yes, but only if the load requires placards

questions.explanation: The exception covers material transported "By the shipper as a private carrier except for a hazardous material that is to be reshipped or transferred from one carrier to another." Without an exception, "each person who offers a hazardous material for transportation shall certify".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.204, Shipper's certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 172.205(c), whose dates and handwritten signatures must the original copy of the hazardous waste manifest bear?

options.A: The person representing the shipper (generator) when the waste is offered, and the person representing the initial carrier accepting it
options.B: Only the designated facility receiving the waste
options.C: Only the driver, at the time of delivery
options.D: Only an EPA official

questions.explanation: "The original copy of the manifest must be dated by, and bear the handwritten signature of, the person representing:" the shipper (generator) "at the time it is offered for transportation" and "The initial carrier accepting the waste for transportation."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.205, Hazardous waste manifest (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: What does 172.205(h) say about the hazardous waste manifest and the shipping paper?

options.A: The manifest may never be used as the shipping paper
options.B: The manifest may be used as the shipping paper only for rail shipments
options.C: The manifest takes the place of the emergency response telephone number
options.D: A manifest required by 40 CFR part 262 that contains all of the information required by Subpart C may be used as the shipping paper

questions.explanation: "A hazardous waste manifest required by 40 CFR part 262, containing all of the information required by this subpart, may be used as the shipping paper required by this subpart."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.205, Hazardous waste manifest (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: How does 172.602(c)(1) require a carrier transporting a hazardous material by highway to maintain the emergency response information?

options.A: Only at the carrier's main office
options.B: Packed inside the package with the hazardous material
options.C: In the same manner as prescribed for shipping papers, immediately accessible to the driver
options.D: Only as an electronic file sent after an incident

questions.explanation: Each carrier "shall maintain the information specified in paragraph (a) of this section and § 172.606 of this part in the same manner as prescribed for shipping papers", and it "must be immediately accessible to train crew personnel, drivers of motor vehicles, flight crew members, and bridge personnel on vessels".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.602, Emergency response information (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which item is part of the minimum emergency response information listed in 172.602(a)?

options.A: The driver's name and CDL number
options.B: Preliminary first aid measures
options.C: The consignee's delivery hours
options.D: The planned route

questions.explanation: Emergency response information "as a minimum, must contain" items that include "Immediate hazards to health", "Risks of fire or explosion" and "Preliminary first aid measures."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.602, Emergency response information (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Emergency response telephone number and carrier contact
questions.question: Which emergency response telephone number meets 172.604(a)?

options.A: An answering service that takes a message and calls back
options.B: A beeper number
options.C: An answering machine that is checked once a day
options.D: A number, monitored at all times the material is in transportation, of a person knowledgeable of the material who has comprehensive emergency response and incident mitigation information for it

questions.explanation: The number must be that of a person "knowledgeable of the hazardous material being shipped and has comprehensive emergency response and incident mitigation information for that material" (or with immediate access to such a person). "A telephone number that requires a call back (such as an answering service, answering machine, or beeper device) does not meet the requirements of paragraph (a) of this section".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.604, Emergency response telephone number (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Emergency response telephone number and carrier contact
questions.question: An offeror wants to enter the emergency response telephone number once on the shipping paper, in a prominent and clearly visible manner, instead of immediately after the description. When does 172.604(a)(3)(ii) allow this?

options.A: Only if the number applies to each hazardous material on the shipping paper and it is indicated that the number is for emergency response information
options.B: Whenever the shipping paper has more than one page
options.C: Only for hazardous waste shipments
options.D: Whenever the carrier, not the offeror, prepared the shipping paper

questions.explanation: "The offeror may use one of the methods prescribed in this paragraph only if the telephone number applies to each hazardous material entered on the shipping paper, and if it is indicated that the telephone number is for emergency response information".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.604, Emergency response telephone number (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Emergency response telephone number and carrier contact
questions.question: A semi-trailer holding hazardous material that needs a shipping paper is separated from its tractor and parked somewhere other than a facility operated by the consignor or consignee or a facility subject to 172.602(c)(2). It is not marked with the identification numbers described in 172.606(c). What must the carrier do under 172.606(b)?

options.A: Nothing, because the trailer is no longer attached to motive power
options.B: Notify the consignee within 24 hours
options.C: One of two options: mark the trailer with the motor carrier's telephone number on the front exterior near the brake hose and electrical connections (or on a label, tag or sign attached there), or have the shipping paper and emergency response information readily available on the trailer
options.D: Remove the shipping paper from the trailer

questions.explanation: The carrier shall "Mark the transport vehicle with the telephone number of the motor carrier on the front exterior near the brake hose and electrical connections" (or on a label, tag or sign there), or "Have the shipping paper and emergency response information readily available on the transport vehicle."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.606, Carrier information contact (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Emergency response telephone number and carrier contact
questions.question: Under 172.606(a), who must instruct the driver of a motor vehicle to contact the carrier in the event of an incident involving the hazardous material?

options.A: The shipper (offeror)
options.B: Each carrier who transports or accepts for transportation a hazardous material for which a shipping paper is required
options.C: The consignee
options.D: The emergency response information provider

questions.explanation: "Each carrier who transports or accepts for transportation a hazardous material for which a shipping paper is required shall instruct the operator of a motor vehicle, train, aircraft, or vessel to contact the carrier (e.g., by telephone or mobile radio) in the event of an incident involving the hazardous material."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.606, Carrier information contact (as of Nov 4, 2026)
